message.abstract: <jats:p>This work reports the development of an electrode material derived from bamboo stem via NaOH activation, integrating hierarchical porosity, and surface functionalization for electrochemical capacitor applications. The synthesized carbon exhibits a flaky, fibrous morphology with micro–mesoporous networks as confirmed by SEM, and a predominantly amorphous structure with short-range graphitic ordering from XRD. Elemental analysis via EDS reveals a high carbon content (94.65%) and nitrogen content (3.4%), which enhances charge storage and electrical conductivity. BET and BJH analyses indicate a high surface area (865–1147 m²/g), a pore volume of 0.552 cm³/g, and an average pore diameter of 2.43 nm, favourable for ion diffusion and electrolyte access. Electrochemical testing demonstrates a high specific capacitance of 833 F/g at 0.5 A/g, attributed to combined electric double-layer capacitance and pseudocapacitive contributions from oxygen- and nitrogen-containing functional groups, as evidenced by FTIR and CV (b = 0.787; 21% diffusion-controlled contribution). Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy shows a low equivalent series resistance of 0.2 Ω, while charge–discharge cycling confirms excellent stability with 94% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles. The CV and GCD further confirm its potency for efficient charge transport and high energy storage performance. These findings highlight the potential of bamboo-derived activated carbon as a sustainable and cost-effective electrode material. However, the overall energy and power densities remain constrained by the narrow voltage window of the aqueous electrolyte and the limited cycling evaluation, indicating the need for further study with other electrolytes with higher voltage window and long-term testing.</jats:p>
title: NaOH-Activated Bamboo Carbon with Hierarchical Porosity for High-Performance Electrochemical Capacitors
